title: Data Mapper

validation.research: Six authoritative source notes. Fowler’s Data Mapper entry in Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture establishes separate object/database representation transfer with a domain model independent of persistence and the mapper. Active Record supplies the responsibility contrast; Identity Map is treated as an additional pattern. Official SQLAlchemy documentation shows imperative/declarative mapper configuration and the separate expected-version mechanism for stale updates. Official Python SQLite documentation supports caller-owned transaction and connection handling. The appointment example and native illustrations are original teaching material. No ORM dependency or neighboring candidate stub was added.
validation.python_examples: All three actual article fences execute as model.py, mapper.py, and demo.py and produce six stated lines exactly. Checks verify that the model imports only dataclasses, start/end and start/duration round-trip inversely, loaded objects retain overlap behavior, midnight/day-end and full-day intervals are valid, empty/reversed/out-of-range/noninteger intervals reject, half-open adjacency is not overlap, independent immutable loads have explicit identity semantics, exact ASCII IDs preserve quotes and whitespace, missing loads return None, missing updates raise LookupError, unchanged-row updates succeed, duplicates and operational failures propagate, malformed stored intervals reject, insert and update do not commit, caller rollback restores writes, multiple operations roll back together, and committed state is visible through another connection. An explicit stale-object update overwrites later state, verifying the documented absence of version protection rather than implying concurrency safety.

example_limits: Python 3.10+ and standard-library SQLite. Appointment and TimeSlot are immutable snapshots with exact nonblank ASCII IDs and whole minutes in one abstract local day, using half-open intervals in [0,1440]. The mapper supports find, insert, and update only, and does not commit or close the caller’s connection. It supplies no deletion, identity map, dirty tracking, calendar dates, time zones, daylight-saving transitions, authorization, scheduling-conflict enforcement, or expected-version check. Its ID-only update can overwrite later state, as explicitly tested. Caller transaction and concurrency policies remain separate from representation transfer. The minimal table permits legacy invalid intervals so reconstruction failures are visible; the domain constructor does not silently repair them.
